headline: High: shared writable workspaces and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; compliance risk is also elevated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can read/write files and its skills “reference each other and build on shared context”; Agent B runs in a persistent Replit workspace with read/write filesystem access. That creates a plausible file-based injection bridge even without MCP or clipboard. The pathway is not proven by direct interaction evidence, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Agent B ingests files from the shared Repl workspace as instructions, injection is possible.
IF Agent A writes attacker-controlled content into shared files, B may follow it.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces or directories.
Add a file allowlist for B before reading A-authored artifacts.
Prefix A outputs with machine-readable delimiters and ignore free text.
Review any shared-context files before B consumes them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files and enforce them in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A has filesystem read/write plus allowlisted network egress; Agent B touches secrets and deployment configuration and has broad egress. If they share a workspace, A can read sensitive files and B can transmit them outward. Because B’s profile explicitly includes secrets handling and broad egress, the leakage blast radius is substantial.
conditions: IF the two agents operate on the same Repl workspace, A can access files B touches.
IF secrets or deployment configs are present in that workspace, either agent can expose them via network egress.
mitigations: Move secrets out of any shared workspace.
Restrict B’s egress to a deny-by-default proxy.
Store sensitive files in a separate mount not visible to A.
Rotate any secrets already present in the shared workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem; B can also modify git state and run subprocesses, while A can spawn subprocesses and write files. In a shared repo or workspace, concurrent edits can corrupt state or overwrite each other, and B’s git operations make the conflict potentially irreversible. The overlap is directly supported by both profiles.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or workspace, concurrent writes can collide.
IF B performs git commits or rebases while A is editing files, state corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize write access with a simple lock file.
Require manual review before B commits git changes.
Snapshot the workspace before parallel runs.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A’s marketing outputs can become B’s inputs if the pair shares files or handoffs, and B is capable of acting on workspace content with shell and git tools. There is no direct evidence that B blindly trusts A, so this is not high, but the default file-based workflow makes unverified propagation plausible.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated files as source material without verification, errors can cascade.
IF A writes incorrect marketing claims into shared artifacts, B may propagate them into code or deployment assets.
mitigations: Require B to verify A outputs against source data.
Keep A-generated content in a review-only folder.
Add a human approval step before B acts on A outputs.
Use explicit schema validation for handoff files.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware gating between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Replit environment, while Agent A is a marketing skill with allowlisted network egress and filesystem access. If regulated or confidential data enters the shared workspace, the pair can create residency/retention and secret-handling mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific regulation breach, so high—not critical—is warranted.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is placed in the shared workspace, B’s secret-handling and cloud execution become compliance-sensitive.
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the workspace, the pair may violate them.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Document data residency and retention for both agents.
Disable secret storage in any shared files.
Review vendor terms before placing PII in Replit.
requires-engineering: segregate compliance-bound workloads by environment.
